 SAMHI Hotels reports 15.6 per cent growth in Q2 FY27 total income
 3 min read SAMHI The company reported an EBITDA margin of 39.1 per cent, excluding the impact of changes in Goods and Services Tax (GST) regulations 
 SAMHI Hotels Limited reported a 15.6 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated total income to Rs 342.7 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 296.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Consolidated EBITDA increased 12 per cent to Rs 123.8 crore from Rs 110.5 crore, while the reported EBITDA margin stood at 36.1 per cent. 
 On a same-store basis, revenue grew 12.6 per cent year-on-year, exceeding the company's long-term guidance of 9 to 11 per cent. Occupancy rose to 78.6 per cent from 75 per cent in Q2 FY26, while revenue per available room (RevPAR) grew 14.3 per cent, supported by a 9.2 per cent increase in average room rate (ARR). Domestic travellers accounted for approximately 80 per cent of the room nights sold during the quarter. 
 The company reported a consolidated EBITDA margin of 39.1 per cent excluding the impact of changes in Goods and Services Tax (GST) regulations. The GST-related impact resulted in a 300-basis-point dilution, bringing the reported margin to 36.1 per cent. Comparable EBITDA growth, excluding the GST impact, stood at 21.3 per cent year-on-year. 
 Profit before tax (PBT) before exceptional items increased 39.9 per cent to Rs 53.4 crore. Reported PBT stood at Rs 57.3 crore, compared with Rs 119.7 crore in Q2 FY26, a decline of 52.1 per cent. Profit after tax (PAT) was Rs 41.1 crore, down 58.8 per cent from Rs 99.8 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Reported PAT included exceptional gains of Rs 3.9 crore in Q2 FY27 and Rs 84.1 crore in Q2 FY26. PAT excluding exceptional items stood at Rs 37.2 crore, up 136.9 per cent year-on-year. Free cash flow was Rs 82.7 crore. 
 As of September 30, 2026, SAMHI's net debt stood at Rs 1,457.9 crore, compared with Rs 1,450.7 crore as of March 31, 2026. The net debt-to-EBITDA ratio was 3.1x, while the ratio adjusted for growth capital stood at 2.2x. The effective interest rate was 7.8 per cent, approximately 300 basis points lower than at the time of the company's initial public offering. 
 Commenting on the performance,  Ashish Jakhanwala, MD & CEO, SAMHI Hotels Ltd., said, “We are pleased to report our performance for the quarter. Occupancy held close to 80% and RevPAR grew by about 14%, making this a reassuring period for the business. Revenue growth remained ahead of our long-term guidance. Domestic travellers accounted for about 80% of the room nights sold during the quarter. This cohort has proven more resilient amid ongoing geopolitical instability, reinforcing our confidence in the resilience of the Indian economy and the opportunity it represents. 
 Against this strong backdrop, we have been steadily building for the future. For several quarters, our reported growth has been largely driven by same-store performance, as no new inventory came online. This is set to change. We look forward to opening the W Hotel in Hyderabad next fiscal year and have secured a pipeline of approximately 1,700 new rooms through FY2031. These initiatives put us on a path to strong growth, and our focus now is on delivering them on schedule. 
 We are equally proud of having built this pipeline without compromising our discipline: we add assets only in core markets and at a discount to replacement cost. We are not buying growth through expensive acquisitions; instead, we are building it through the efforts that conversions and turnarounds demand, as demonstrated in Bangalore, and by securing long-term leases, as in Noida and Hyderabad. 
 Our modest investment in RARE, together with ongoing discussions on a partnership with Marriott, will help RARE build a strong platform in experience-led leisure across the region, with limited capital exposure. 
 We expect H2 FY27 to be operationally stronger. Going forward, incremental EBITDA is expected to translate into free cash flow, with interest outflows remaining stable. This should enable us to increasingly fund future growth investments through internal cash generation, supporting a disproportionate improvement in free cash flow generation. 
 We released our first Sustainability Report for FY2025-26, covering 31 hotels and 4,899 rooms across 11 states. The report highlights improvements in energy efficiency, waste reduction and renewable energy usage. Building on our FY30 commitments, we will establish quantified targets across key sustainability parameters, with clear baselines to track and benchmark our progress.” 
 SAMHI Hotels Limited has a portfolio of 31 operating hotels comprising 4,899 keys across 13 cities in India, including the National Capital Region (NCR), Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Pune. The company has long-term management arrangements with Marriott, IHG and Hyatt.
